contract.reader: An engineer or student who can build and solve a discretization (entries 1 to 4) and must now say how far a simulation result can be trusted
contract.problem: How to show a code solves its equations correctly, how large the numerical error of one result is without an exact solution, and what a comparison with measurement proves about the model
contract.outcome: Run an observed-order test with a manufactured solution; compute observed order, Richardson extrapolate and GCI from three grids with the asymptotic-range check; form E = S - D and u_val and read E +/- 2u_val; list what a simulation report must state
contract.contribution: Each procedure demonstrated by a script on the series' own problems: a planted indexing bug that still converges at order 1, a GCI tested against a Fourier-series reference, and a hypothetical validation case where input uncertainty limits the conclusion
contract.evidence: Three scripts with real output; AIAA G-077-1998; ASME V&V 10-2006 and 20-2009; JCGM 100:2008 and 101:2008; Oberkampf and Roy; Richardson 1911; Roache 1994 and 1998
contract.limitations: Steady scalar quantities of interest on smooth problems; the validation case is hypothetical; model-form uncertainty and validation hierarchies described, not computed
